newsitem.title: THAILAND: Cambodian ministers meet Khmer Rouge's Ieng Sary.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian ministers meet Khmer Rouge's Ieng Sary.

text.p: Cambodia's co-defence ministers met top dissident Khmer Rouge leader Ieng Sary in Bangkok on Thursday and discussed prospects for national reconciliation with the breakaway group, one of the ministers said.

"We have met and held frank discussions in a good and sincere atmosphere. The meeting was successful and we agreed to consider amnesty for him (Ieng Sary)," co-defence minister Tea Banh told reporters at his hotel in the Thai capital.
Ieng Sary heads a faction that last month split from the Maoist Khmer Rouge guerrilla group led by Pol Pot.

He was foreign minister during the Khmer Rouge reign of terror in the 1970s in which more than a million Cambodians died of disease, starvation or overwork in labour camps, and was sentenced to death in absentia for his role in the genocide.
Ieng Sary, who is based in western Cambodia, has been seeking a royal pardon from Cambodia since he broke from the main group.

"He (Ieng Sary) has made a major contribution for the unity and reconciliation of Cambodia by breaking away from the Khmer Rouge. The government will certainly consider an amnesty for him," Tea Banh said.
Thursday's meeting was the first direct contact between Ieng Sary and high-level Cambodian officials.
